request.rationale: The initial unresolved distinction is whether the official target set contains static branch or Jacobian/limit obstructions, versus failures being caused by sampled-data dynamics and hold stabilization. Exhaustive branch-wise IK with compiled-model forward residuals will resolve the geometric side; compiled masses, actuator transmission, torque-response probes, and free decay will constrain the dynamic interpretation. A finding of infeasible targets or near-singular feasible branches would redirect the campaign toward posture/geometry handling. If targets are feasible with margin and actuation is credible, the next direction should measure or train closed-loop reach-and-hold behavior and diagnose first-entry velocity and interruptions.

request.current_synthesis: Observed in completed operation M1: on a 29-by-72 grid spanning the official radius and angle ranges, all 2088 targets had at least one joint-limit-feasible analytic IK branch; each individual elbow branch was feasible for 1972 of 2088 samples (94.44%), with the excluded samples near shoulder limits. Analytic forward-kinematics residual was at most 1.6e-16 m. Among sampled feasible branch configurations, the smallest Jacobian singular value was 0.0415 m, so the official terminal set is not intrinsically singular. The compiled actuators transmit control directly with gear 5, and unit controls produced 5-unit generalized actuator force with coupled accelerations of roughly 400-490 rad/s^2 at the probe posture. A 1-second zero-control probe reduced initial joint velocities of [1.0,-0.7] rad/s to numerical zero. Interpretation: static position-space impossibility and terminal Jacobian singularity are contradicted as primary explanations for the official goal gap. The branch result supports a branch-selection explanation for edge targets, while the acceleration and damping results support a competing sampled-data reach/braking/hold explanation. M1 did not measure a learned policy, trajectories, first-entry velocity, actuator saturation during a task, limit impulses, sub-control-step excursions, or protected hold semantics; therefore it cannot rank those closed-loop explanations or establish success.
request.decision_frontier: The unresolved scientific distinction is whether the dominant attainable-policy limitation is (a) target-conditioned branch/joint-limit selection, especially near the approximately 170-degree shoulder boundary, or (b) dynamic closed-loop behavior after choosing a feasible posture: reach time, braking, residual velocity, and repeated exits during the 100-sample hold. Evidence that failure clusters at limit-margin targets or that branch-conditioned trajectories differ materially would direct the campaign toward posture-aware control and distribution coverage. Evidence that failures occur across feasible branches with high first-entry velocity, actuator saturation, or hold interruptions would direct it toward braking/stabilization and hold-aware learning. A policy evaluation with synchronized target geometry, first-entry timing and velocity, maximum uninterrupted hold, interruptions, action magnitude, and success is the discriminating test.
request.human_goal_connection: The human goal requires at least 196 of 200 official episodes to complete an uninterrupted 2-second Cartesian hold. M1 establishes that the target positions are statically reachable in the compiled robot, so progress should focus on learning a controller that selects feasible postures, traverses them, brakes residual velocity, and preserves the hold across the full radius-angle distribution.

The unchanged scenario mechanics and reward retain reach, braking-through-dynamics, action-saturation, and hold-completion behavior so the subsequent synchronized evaluation can distinguish coverage improvement from persistent control or stabilization limits.

request.description: Evaluate the terminal full-range PPO candidate and the prior outer-range baseline on the same 160-episode research panel, retaining synchronized radius-angle, reach/braking, action-saturation, first-entry, interruption, and complete-success diagnostics.
request.rationale: T2 is the direct full 6-20 cm coverage intervention for I2, but its lower training success than T1 makes evaluation essential rather than inferential. A paired same-seed comparison isolates the recipe outcome on the identical development targets: a sharp reduction in sub-14 cm no-entry failures without worsening trained-range saturation or entered-hold interruptions supports the coverage intervention, while persistent inner-radius failures or hold/control tails redirects the next intervention toward sampled-data braking or stabilization. Neither development result establishes the official 98% goal.

request.description: Aggregate the synchronized M5 diagnostics for the full-range T2 candidate and paired T1 baseline into radius-band, angle-sector, reach/braking, action-saturation, first-entry, and hold-interruption summaries.
request.rationale: T2 improved paired development success from 68.75% to 93.75%, but the remaining ten failures determine whether I2 is supported as a useful coverage intervention or whether sampled-data braking and hold stabilization now limit progress. Applying the existing reach-and-hold analyzer to both same-seed artifacts will quantify the closure criteria without changing evaluation semantics or introducing a new intervention.

request.outcome: The full-range PPO recipe is supported as a major but insufficient intervention. T2 improved the paired development panel from 110/160 to 150/160 successes, eliminated all 23 baseline no-entry failures in 6-10 cm, reduced 10-14 cm no-entry failures from 15 to 3, and reduced entered failures from 8 to 3 without worsening the failed-episode action-saturation tail.
request.reason: M5 and M6 establish the recipe outcome but not the 98% official goal or a universal causal claim. T2 still had 10 failures in 160 episodes, equivalent to 12.5 failures per 200, so the at-most-four-failure target was not reached. The remaining failures were 7 no-entry episodes, including 4 in the trained 14-20 cm range with approximately 496-498 saturated action steps, plus 3 entered-but-incomplete holds with 435 total interruptions. Full-range exposure therefore resolved the dominant inner-radius distribution gap, while the residual decision frontier moves to sampled-data/directional reach-braking control and hold stabilization.

pi_checkpoint.candidates_and_roles: T1 produced candidates through 120,832 completed steps, including T1:checkpoint-120832, but no working, best-known, or retained model role is assigned. The candidate remains a diagnostic baseline only; its 68.75% development-panel result is not official assessment evidence.
pi_checkpoint.cumulative_resource_use: M1 characterization completed; T1 requested 120,000 training steps and completed 120,832; M2 evaluated 160 development episodes; M3 aggregated M2; E2 opened I1 and E4 reframed I1; M4 stratified M2 by radius and angle; E7 closed I1; E9 opened I2. No official assessment requested.
pi_checkpoint.current_goal_gap: No policy is near the 98% goal. T1's 68.75% development success comprised 42 no-entry failures and 8 entered-but-incomplete holds. M4 is development evidence only and does not establish official success. The remaining gap is to train and evaluate a policy covering 6-20 cm while reducing the secondary difficult-angle reach/braking tail and entered-hold instability to no more than four failures in the official 200-episode assessment.
pi_checkpoint.current_synthesis: Established observations: M1 found at least one joint-limit-feasible analytic IK branch for every sampled official target, feasible terminal postures were not intrinsically singular, and the compiled actuators had substantial authority with free velocity decay. T1/M2 measured 110/160 successes under training radii 14-20 cm. M3 found 42 no-entry failures and 8 entered-but-incomplete holds; every no-entry target had a feasible analytic branch, so branch feasibility is not the primary cause of the dominant failure class, while entered failures had hold interruptions and much higher action saturation. M4 found 23/23 no-entry failures in 6-10 cm, 15/15 in 10-14 cm, 2/39 in 14-18 cm, and 2/28 in 18-20 cm, so 38/42 no-entry failures were below the 14 cm training boundary. The four trained-range no-entry failures had approximately 1.2-1.4 cm minimum distances, 2.9 m/s maximum end-effector speed, 500 saturated action steps, and negative-angle concentration. Interpretation: inner-radius distribution shift is the primary pre-entry mechanism in this development panel, with a consequential secondary sampled-data reach/braking or directional-control tail; the eight entered failures remain consistent with a separate hold-stability mechanism. E7 closed I1 because M4 met its closure condition. E9 opened I2; this records the selected intervention question, not evidence that full-range training is causal or sufficient. Limits: all results are development evidence from 160 episodes; they do not establish intervention causality or the 98% official goal.
pi_checkpoint.decision_frontier: I1 is closed and I2 is opened. The unresolved distinction is whether the dominant inner-radius no-entry failures are chiefly a learnable distribution-coverage gap or instead persist because of sampled-data reach/braking, directional control, or post-entry hold instability. A fresh candidate trained over the full official 6-20 cm distribution and evaluated with synchronized radius-angle, reach/braking, saturation, first-entry, interruption, and complete-success diagnostics will discriminate these routes: a sharp reduction below 14 cm without worsening trained-range saturation or entered-hold interruptions supports the tested recipe's usefulness, while persistent inner-radius failures, increased trained-range saturation, or continuing hold interruptions redirects the next intervention toward the corresponding control or stabilization mechanism. Neither outcome alone establishes or invalidates the broader learning method.
pi_checkpoint.human_goal_connection: The human goal requires at least 196 of 200 official episodes to complete an uninterrupted 2-second Cartesian hold. The baseline achieved 110/160 on development evidence, leaving 50 failures. Closing I1 identified the dominant 42-failure pre-entry mechanism, and E9 opened I2 to test whether full official-radius coverage reduces that failure tail before any official assessment.
pi_checkpoint.next_direction_or_closure: The goal-review transition is complete. Continue in fresh inquiry I2 by training a fresh PPO candidate with full 6-20 cm radius coverage while retaining difficult-angle exposure and control-aware reach, braking, and uninterrupted-hold behavior, then evaluate it on the synchronized development panel. Do not assign a role or request official assessment until the inquiry evidence establishes whether the candidate materially closes the failure gap.
pi_checkpoint.next_question: Does a fresh PPO candidate trained over the full official 6-20 cm radius distribution, while retaining difficult-angle exposure and control-aware reach, braking, and uninterrupted-hold behavior, materially reduce inner-radius no-entry failures and the trained-range saturation tail toward at most four failures per 200 episodes?
